Voor de uitvoering van primaire taken zoals afvalinzameling, stadsreiniging, groenvoorziening, handhaving en sportveldonderhoud, evenals zakelijke vervoersbewegingen van medewerkers, maakt de gemeente gebruik van meer dan 1.000 voertuigen. Deze voertuigen worden gedeeld door een wisselende groep van ruim 6.000 medewerkers en leggen gezamenlijk jaarlijks meer dan 10 miljoen kilometers af. Om het wagenpark van de gemeente effectief te kunnen beheren is er behoefte aan een gedetailleerd inzicht in de status en gebruik van elk voertuig en betrouwbaar toegangsbeheer. Om te kunnen voldoen aan wettelijke verplichtingen en om efficiëntie en duurzaamheid te bevorderen, maakt de gemeente gebruik van voertuigtelematica. Deze technologie combineert hardware in voertuigen met telecommunicatie (zoals 4G/5G, GPS en Bluetooth), analyse-software (SaaS) en persoonlijke devices (zoals apps of tags). Hiermee kunnen voertuigen op afstand worden uitgelezen en geanalyseerd, en kan de toegang tot voertuigen effectief worden beheerd. Door de inzet van voertuigtelematica kan real -time en op afstand een veelheid aan voertuigdata worden ontsloten aan de wagenparkbeheerders. Die data kunnen worden gebruikt om te kunnen sturen op inzet voertuigen (bezettingsgraad), onderhoud, brandstofverbruik e.d. en er kan mee worden voldaan aan wettelijke eisen van registratie en monitoring. Doel van deze aanbesteding is om voor een langere periode een samenwerking aan te gaan met een leverancier die de gemeente optimaal kan ondersteunen en ontzorgen op het gebied van voertuigtelematica voor vrijwel alle ca. 1.000 voertuigen van de gemeente.

This public contract will be implemented as part of the SLIM (Sustainable Landscape through Integrated Management) Project, which is being implemented by the Czech Development Agency from October 2023 to September 2027 and co-financed by the European Union and Sweden. Its aim is to introduce an integrated landscape management (ILM) approach and contribute to increasing the resilience of ecosystems and preserving biodiversity in Zambia using freely accessible satellite data in areas such as forestry, agriculture, water management, and environmental protection, including predicting and mitigating the destructive effects of natural disasters. This contract will specifically contribute to the implementation of the SLIM project activity entitled "Provision of adequate technological capacities, tools, data access, and geospatial data storage infrastructure for the crucial data domains." The subject of this contract is the supply, installation, and commissioning of ICT infrastructure and equipment required to support the SLIM project in Zambia. The contract will deliver the hardware infrastructure necessary for geospatial data storage, processing, and access across participating government institutions, together with the related installation, configuration, testing, training, and handover services. A central component of the contract is the deployment of two server environments supporting geospatial data management. The first server solution will be installed at the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) and will support a centralized GIS platform based on the ArcGIS Enterprise ecosystem for the storage, management, analysis, and publication of satellite imagery and other environmental datasets. The second server solution will be delivered to the Forestry Department and will support an open-source GIS platform built on PostgreSQL/PostGIS, MapServer, and QGIS technologies, enabling internal forestry data management and web-based geospatial services. In addition to the server infrastructure, the contract includes the supply of end-user computing equipment and large-format devices required for geospatial analysis and operational use. This includes laptops, desktop computers, specialized workstations, A0 scanners, and an A0 plotter distributed among several participating institutions. The contract also covers installation and configuration of all equipment, implementation of baseline security settings, system testing, training of administrators and end users, and final commissioning and handover to the beneficiary institutions. The subject matter of this contract is described in more detail in Annex No. 1 – "Supply Specification".

Der Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Ruhr (VRR) zählt zu den fahrgaststärksten Verkehrsverbünden Europas. Rund zwei Drittel aller Bushaltestellen im VRR sind bislang nicht barrierefrei ausgebaut. Zur Beschleunigung des barrierefreien Ausbaus beabsichtigen der VRR sowie die beteiligten kommunalen Straßenbaulastträger die Vergabe von Vermessungen und Planungsleistungen in Anlehnung an die HOAI-Leistungsphasen 1 bis 9 für insgesamt 558 Bushaltestellensteige im Verbundgebiet. Das Projektgebiet umfasst folgende Kommunen und Kreise: Bottrop, Dortmund, Duisburg, Düsseldorf, Emmerich am Rhein, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Gevelsberg, Gladbeck, Grefrath, Hagen, Haltern am See, Hattingen, Jüchen, Kerken, Meerbusch, Remscheid, Schermbeck, Solingen, Sprockhövel, Viersen, Waltrop, Wetter (Ruhr), Willich, Wülfrath, Wuppertal sowie den Ennepe-Ruhr-Kreis. Diese Kommunen und Kreise sind vorläufig in sieben regionale Lose aufgeteilt. Die konkrete Aufteilung ist der Leistungsbeschreibung (Anlage 02) zu entnehmen. Darüber hinaus sind weitere Anmerkungen zur Loseinteilung in der Anlage 04 zusammengefasst worden.

Description of Work and Services to be Provided: structured around eight work packages (WPs) covering the full cycle from system design through operationalization, capacity development, and digital enablement. WP1: Inception, Alignment, and Mobilization. It establishes the analytical and operational foundation for the assignment. The contractor reviews and consolidates the OECD/Sigma diagnostic findings, conducts targeted design assessments to collect operational information required for subsequent WPs, including data feasibility mapping, institutional baseline mapping, planning-budgeting process validation, pilot site readiness assessment, and a digital systems inventory. The contractor establishes the governance and coordination arrangements, detailed workplan, stakeholder engagement plan, and risk register. The primary deliverable is a comprehensive Inception Report. WP2: National M&E System Framework and Governance. It produces the foundational design of the national M&E system, developed jointly with MoFP and key government stakeholders rather than as an externally designed product. It defines the system"s purpose, scope, institutional roles, governance mechanisms, core M&E processes, data governance principles, integration logic with planning and budgeting, evaluation framework, and system stewardship mandate. The deliverable is a government-endorsed National M&E Framework. WP3: Results and Measurement Architecture. It redesigns the Strategic Results Framework using a methodology-first, pilot-based approach that accounts for the current limitations of the national development plan. The contractor develops a comprehensive SRF methodology and standards framework designed for the next national planning cycle, conducts a participatory results clarification exercise with a pilot of sectors, and produces a transitional indicator set for the remaining current planning cycle to enable piloting. Deliverables include the revised SRF Methodology Document and the Updated SRF and Indicator Framework. WP4: Institutional and Functional Design. It defines the organizational arrangements required to anchor M&E and data management as permanent government functions. Through a participatory process with MoFP and LMAs, the contractor develops functional design models, organizational options with feasibility assessments against General Personnel Council (GCP) civil service frameworks, RACI matrices, workflow systems, and HR alignment proposals. The deliverable is an Institutional and Functional Design Report. WP5: Integration with Planning, Budgeting, and Oversight. It defines how M&E information can flow into and influences core government decision-making processes, including annual planning, budget preparation, and performance oversight at CoM level. The contractor maps actual planning and budgeting processes, assesses linkage feasibility, designs standard decision-informing M&E products, and proposes integration mechanisms. Deliverables include M&E Integration Framework and Updated Planning and Budgeting Guidance Notes. WP6: Operationalization and Piloting. It translates the system design into operational reality through co-developed SOPs, data collection instruments, reporting templates, and interim digital tools, tested with 3-5 pilot LMAs selected on the basis of a readiness assessment conducted in WP1. The pilot tests real workflows and data flows, generating feedback that is incorporated into system refinements. The deliverable is a Pilot Implementation Report. WP7: Capacity Development, Change Management, and Sustainability. It builds the professional and institutional capacities required for sustained system operation. The contractor develops competency frameworks, training programs, and materials; delivers training in two waves; designs and initiates change management and communication strategies; proposes institutionalization and incentive mechanisms in coordination with GPC; and, importantly, builds system stewardship capacity enabling MoFP and LMAs to maintain, update, and evolve the system independently after assignment conclusion. Deliverables include the Capacity Development and Change Management Strategy, Competency Frameworks and Training Roadmap, Training Modules and Materials, System Stewardship Package, and System Handover and Transition Protocol. WP8: Digital Enablement Design and Procurement-Ready Specifications. It produces the complete technical basis for procuring a digital M&E platform. The contractor defines functional requirements, designs the data architecture and interoperability framework, conducts a technology options assessment including AI and emerging technology analysis, designs a public results portal concept, and produces a vendor-neutral technical and procurement specifications package.

Clare, including all associated site works and ancillary development. The project involves a comprehensive retrofit of the existing building to improve thermal performance, accessibility and fire safety standards. Works include the removal of selected internal elements, reconfiguration of internal layouts, and installation of new partitions, doors and finishes throughout. Energy upgrade works include the installation of an external wall insulation (ETICS) system, upgraded attic insulation, new high-performance windows and doors, improved airtightness measures, installation of a new air-to-water heat pump system with associated pipework and controls, mechanical ventilation upgrades, and the provision of a roof-mounted solar photovoltaic (PV) system. Mechanical and electrical works include a full rewire, upgrades to heating and hot water systems, installation and modification of fire detection and alarm systems, emergency lighting, and associated building services. The works also include the conversion and upgrade of an existing detached garage structure to provide ancillary office accommodation (PIC Office), including insulation, new windows and doors, roofing works, and associated mechanical and electrical installations. External works comprise new and upgraded pathways, ramps and hardstanding areas, drainage improvements, installation of soakaways and sustainable drainage features, and all associated site development works. All works are to be carried out in accordance with the Building Surveyor’s drawings and specification, and in compliance with current Building Regulations and relevant standards.
